supersedes: protocol.json (v1 realtime native cohort: comparison invalid, see results.json)
question: Under synchronous execution, does --fine-gain-schedule shorten fine alignment SIM time and whole-mission SIM time without losing physical/protocol success?
why_synchronous: v1 realtime runs were dominated by host CPU load (SIM/wall 0.575-0.95). Without --realtime-control, physics waits for each capture and decision, so host load changes wall time but not actor inputs, decisions or SIM time.

runtime.source: HEAD at launch, committed and clean (recorded per run)

design.host_load: recorded before each run; not a precondition because it does not affect SIM-time metrics

fixed.stage_and_grasp_models: outputs/dispatch-models/e78a5a5777f5bc48/models/{varied,grasp} (faster-dispatch worktree copy; file hashes identical to the v19 simulation-realtime copy used by the replay audit)

command_template: bash scripts/open_simulation.command dispatch --headless --plan-replay experiments/2026-09-22-parallel-transport/independent-plan.json --variant open --seed 11 --contact-profile local_contact_fine --max-wall-s 1200 --overlap-start grasp --video-fps 10 --grasp-model-dir <models>/grasp --stage-model-dir <models>/varied [--fine-gain-schedule] --output /Users/changmin/projects/ugrp/outputs/fine-gain-schedule-20260924-sync/<run>
primary_metrics: fine alignment SIM s (learned_approach approach_elapsed_sim_s) and per-stage movement slices
secondary_metrics: coarse sample count, box pregrasp resource wait
acceptance: Both B runs physically and protocol complete
Report per-run B vs A fine SIM s and control_end_sim_s; never average incomplete runs
No realtime-window speed claim; default adoption out of scope
stop_conditions: A B failure skips remaining B runs; A2 still runs
No budget extension or threshold change
limits: One saved plan, open map, seed 11; not a generalization or real-robot claim
Response constants are a controller calibration from recorded RGB-derived error changes, not a physical measurement
Box approach may become the critical path once the beam fine stage shortens; its tilt-step limit is handled separately in draft PRs #129/#131
Synchronous mode measures SIM-time behavior; realtime native wall time needs a separate idle-host check
